We've admitted only a handful of children and none have been severely ill. This pattern holds true nationally as well. There have been a few pediatric deaths nationally due to COVID, but the flu remains a much bigger player for children. Again I stress the need for flu vaccination in the fall for the entire family as COVID may again spike up just as flu emerges in the late fall.

More data has emerged on adult infections and reinforces that comorbidities and age are the biggest risk factors for severe disease. > 50% admitted to ICU's are 65 years and older. Under 60 year old risk factors are obesity, hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, immunosuppression (chemotherapy) to name a few. Interestingly, asthma does not appear to increase risk for severe disease. The middle age and healthy are still getting ill and are hospitalized, but are in the minority (<10 %).

In my opinion, it is time to loosen the social restrictions and open up the economy in an intelligent and controlled manner. This may cause another spike down the road but our hospital system is in a good place to manage this if it does occur. Hospitals have started doing elective surgical cases today on a small scale. Retail will open on a small scale in the near future and hopefully restaurants will be allowed to open in the next couple of weeks with reduced seating. At risk individuals should continue to be very careful and maintain social distancing until we know if cases will spike when things start reopening.
